title: Is the gait rhythm deterministic? Recurrence quantification and entropy of real ankle accelerometry

dataset.name: PAMAP2 Physical Activity Monitoring Data Set
dataset.record: subject 101, ankle IMU acceleration (+/-16g) vector magnitude @ 100 Hz; walking / running / vacuuming / ironing (<= 2500 samples each)
dataset.citation: Reiss A, Stricker D. Introducing a New Benchmarked Dataset for Activity Monitoring. 16th IEEE ISWC, 2012. UCI ML Repository doi:10.24432/C5NW2H (CC-BY 4.0).

proposition: Lyapunov and sample entropy describe a signal's dynamics; recurrence quantification and approximate entropy say how DETERMINISTIC and REGULAR it is. On real ankle accelerometry the ecosystem separates rhythmic locomotion from aperiodic activity: walking is highly deterministic and regular (RQA determinism 0.921, approximate entropy 0.455), running even more so (determinism 0.983), while aperiodic ironing is neither (determinism 0.382, approximate entropy 1.280) -- a determinism gap of 0.54 and an entropy gap of 0.83 between walking and ironing.

claims.statement: RQA determinism of walking ankle acceleration (quasi-periodic)

validation.reference: Rhythmic human locomotion (walking, running) produces quasi-periodic, deterministic accelerometry -- high recurrence determinism and laminarity and low approximate/sample entropy -- because each stride recurs; aperiodic upper-limb activity (ironing) does not. Recurrence quantification and entropy measures must SEPARATE the two, ordering locomotion as more deterministic and more regular than aperiodic activity.
validation.data: REAL -- PAMAP2 (UCI #231), subject 101, ankle accelerometer @ 100 Hz across four activities
validation.note: The measures cleanly separate rhythmic from aperiodic movement on real data: running (DET 0.983) and walking (DET 0.921) are far more deterministic than ironing (DET 0.382), and walking's approximate entropy (0.455) is far below ironing's (1.280); sample entropy tells the same story (walking 0.035 vs ironing 2.43, in regularity_table.csv). The determinism gap (walk-iron) is 0.54 and the entropy gap (iron-walk) is 0.83. Honest scope: (1) these quantify GAIT-RHYTHM regularity of a continuous accelerometer signal, not orbital stability -- Floquet multipliers need multi-stride joint-angle state vectors, a separate method; (2) values depend on the embedding (m=4, tau=8) and recurrence threshold (target RR=0.1), held fixed across activities so the COMPARISON is fair; (3) one subject, illustrating the method's discrimination, not a population norm.

open_questions.q: Orbital stability of the gait limit cycle (Floquet multipliers) and long-range stride-interval correlations (DFA) are complementary nonlinear-gait markers that need segmented multi-stride kinematics / stride-time series rather than a raw accelerometer window. Documented, not escalated.
